\begin{document}
\begin{center}
{\Large\bfseries Exact multiplication table}\par\medskip
{\large A 111-dimensional algebra with $t_5=0$ and $e_{13}\ne0$}
\end{center}
\textbf{Note from Ois\'{i}n: As one might imagine from the length, this document was almost completely typeset by AI. 
Some rational coefficients have more than 18,000 characters.
This poses a problem:the fidelity of the multiplication table to in this pdf transcription to the original m2 file in particular cannot be hand-checked for obvious reasons.
To solve this, we have a python program which parses both and checks that they agree and this python program can be checked by hand.
This is included in the repo.
}

The basis is $b_0,\ldots,b_{110}$. Multiplication is bilinear and commutative.
Every nonzero product $b_i b_j$ with $i\le j$ is listed below. 
Any omitted products should be taken to be zero.
 The nonzero 13-Engel product is
\begin{equation*}
 x=b_5,\qquad y=b_0,\qquad R_y^{13}(x)=b_{110} \ne 0.
\end{equation*}
Here $t_5$ is the sum of the 105 distinct commutative binary trees on five labelled arguments. 
This algebra is 14-Engel by its positive grading.
\subsection*{How to read this document}
The coefficients which are sufficiently small appear directly in the product table.
The larger coefficients are labelled $C_r$ and are defined exactly in the numerator register as $C_r=N_r/D_s$. 
 The denominator register then prints every $D_s$ in full. 
 References to $C_r$ and $D_s$ are clickable.
 \medskip
UnfortThe long appendices are necessary because .
Shared denominators are printed only once.
\medskip

There are 469 nonzero products and 2749 nonzero structure constants.
